# ![](/./assets/img/function.svg)`puter.ai.chat()`

Copy page

Markdown View as Markdown

OpenAI Open in ChatGPT

Anthropic Open in Claude

Websites Puter Apps Node.js Workers

---

Given a prompt returns the completion that best matches the prompt.

## [](#syntax) Syntax

```js
puter.ai.chat(prompt)
puter.ai.chat(prompt, options = {})
puter.ai.chat(prompt, testMode = false, options = {})
puter.ai.chat(prompt, media, testMode = false, options = {})
puter.ai.chat(prompt, [mediaURLArray], testMode = false, options = {})
puter.ai.chat([messages], testMode = false, options = {})
```

## [](#parameters) Parameters

#### [](#prompt-string) `prompt` (String)

A string containing the prompt you want to complete.

#### [](#options-object-optional) `options` (Object) (Optional)

An object containing the following properties:

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | `String` | The model you want to use for the completion. If not specified, defaults to `gpt-5.4-nano`. More than 500 models are available from providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Alibaba Cloud, xAI, Mistral, OpenRouter, Infron, and others. For a full list, see the [AI models list](https://developer.puter.com/ai/models/) page. |
| `serviceSpeed` | `String` | Preferred service speed, `"standard"`, `"fast"`, or `"ultrafast"`. Unavailable speeds fall back from ultrafast to fast, then standard. Omitting it preserves the model's default service. Faster service may cost more. See [Service speed](#service-speed) and [Model-specific features](#model-specific-features). |
| `stream` | `Boolean` | A boolean indicating whether you want to stream the completion. Defaults to `false`. |
| `max_tokens` | `Number` | The maximum number of tokens to generate in the completion. By default, the specific model's maximum is used. |
| `temperature` | `Number` | A number between 0 and 2 indicating the randomness of the completion. Lower values make the output more focused and deterministic, while higher values make it more random. By default, the model's own temperature is used. See [Model-specific features](#model-specific-features). |
| `reasoning_effort` / `reasoning.effort` | `String` | Controls how much effort reasoning models spend thinking. Supported values: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, and `max`. Lower values give faster responses with less reasoning. See [Model-specific features](#model-specific-features). |
| `thinking` | `Object \| null` | Extended-thinking control: `{ type: "adaptive" \| "enabled" \| "disabled" \| "between_tools", budgetTokens?, display? }`. Pass `null` to send no thinking configuration at all (the model's own default); leaving it unset falls back to the legacy derivation from `reasoning_effort`. `budgetTokens` only applies to `type: "enabled"`. |
| `verbosity` / `text.verbosity` | `String` | Controls how long or short responses are. Supported values: `low`, `medium`, and `high`. Lower values give shorter responses. OpenAI models only. |
| `tools` | `Array` | Function definitions the AI can call. See [Function Calling](#function-calling) for details. |
| `toolChoice` | `String \| Object` | Which tool, if any, the model must call. Pass `"auto"` (the model decides), `"none"` (never call a tool), `"required"` (call at least one), or an object naming a specific tool: `{ type: "tool", name: "..." }`. Requires `tools`. |
| `parallelToolCalls` | `Boolean` | Whether the model may call more than one tool in a single turn. Left unset, tool calls run one at a time. |
| `streamToolInput` | `Boolean` | Streaming only. When `true`, a tool call's arguments arrive incrementally as `tool_use_start` / `tool_input_delta` chunks instead of a single `tool_use` chunk once the call completes. |
| `normalize` | `Boolean` | Controls the format of the non-streaming response. See [Response normalization](#response-normalization). |
| `compaction` | `Boolean \| Object` | Opt into inline context compaction for long conversations. See [Compaction](#compaction). |
| `signal` | `AbortSignal` | Abort the request, including while waiting for the next streamed chunk. Cancellation rejects with the signal reason (normally an `AbortError`). |
| `provider` | `String` | Pin the request to a specific provider, for example `openrouter` or `infron`. Without it, Puter selects a provider for the requested model. Call [`puter.ai.listModelProviders()`](/AI/listModelProviders) for the available values, and [`puter.ai.listModels(provider)`](/AI/listModels) for the models a given provider serves. See [Providers](#providers). |
| `fallback` | `Boolean` | Set to `false` to fail the request when the first provider tried fails, instead of retrying it on another provider that serves the same model. Defaults to `true`. See [Providers](#providers). |
| `outputFormat` | `Object` | Constrains the response to a JSON schema: `{ type: "json_schema", schema, name?, strict? }`. |
| `stopSequences` | `Array<String>` | Up to the model's limit of strings; generation stops the moment one of them appears in the output. |

Some models accept additional options or handle these options differently. See [Model-specific features](#model-specific-features).

#### [](#testmode-boolean-optional) `testMode` (Boolean) (Optional)

A boolean indicating whether you want to use the test API. Defaults to `false`. This is useful for testing your code without using up API credits.

#### [](#media-string-file) `media` (String \| File)

A string containing the URL or Puter path of an image or video, or a `File` object containing the media you want to provide as context for the completion.

#### [](#mediaurlarray-array) `mediaURLArray` (Array)

An array of strings containing the URLs of images or videos you want to provide as context for the completion.

#### [](#messages-array) `messages` (Array)

An array of objects containing the messages you want to complete. Each object must have a `role` and a `content` property. The `role` property must be one of `system`, `assistant`, `user`, or `tool`. The `content` property can be:

1. A string containing the message text

2. An array of content objects for multimodal messages

When using an array of content objects, each object can have:

- `type` (String) \- The type of content:

  - `"text"` \- Text content

  - `"file"` \- File content

- `text` (String) \- The text content (required when type is "text")

- `puter_path` (String) \- The path to the file in Puter's file system (required when type is "file")

An example of a valid `messages` parameter with text only:

```js
[
  {
    role: "system",
    content: "Hello, how are you?",
  },
  {
    role: "user",
    content: "I am doing well, how are you?",
  },
];
```

An example with mixed content including files:

```js
[
  {
    role: "user",
    content: [
      {
        type: "file",
        puter_path: "~/Desktop/document.pdf",
      },
      {
        type: "text",
        text: "Please summarize this document",
      },
    ],
  },
];
```

Providing a messages array is especially useful for building chatbots where you want to provide context to the completion.

## [](#return-value) Return value

Returns a `Promise` that resolves to either:

- A [`ChatResponse`](/Objects/chatresponse) object containing the chat response data, or

- An async iterable object of [`ChatResponseChunk`](/Objects/chatresponsechunk) (when `stream` is set to `true`) that you can use with a `for await...of` loop to receive the response in parts as they become available.

Break out of the `for await...of` loop to stop reading a chat stream. When using `new ReadableStream(response)`, call `reader.cancel()` to stop it.

You can also pass an `AbortSignal` to stop waiting for output. See the [stop a stream example](/playground/ai-chat-stop-stream/).

Stopping a stream stops the output your app receives. Once the request has reached the model, the model still finishes its response, and the whole response is billed.

The `ReadableStream` adapter emits text chunks as UTF-8 text. Other chunk types (including usage, tool calls, reasoning and errors) are serialized as JSON followed by a newline. Use the async iterator to receive every chunk as an object.

## [](#errors) Errors

In case of an error, the `Promise` will reject with an error message.

An unrecognized `serviceSpeed` value rejects with `invalid_service_speed`.

For streaming responses, an error from the AI provider is returned as a chunk with `type: "error"` and a `message` describing the failure. This also happens if the provider stops sending the response before it is complete. Check for error chunks in your `for await...of` loop before treating the response as complete.

If the network connection fails after streaming starts, the loop throws `{ message, code: "network_error" }`. Malformed or truncated JSON throws `{ message, code: "invalid_stream_response" }`. If the stream sends nothing for 15 minutes, it throws `{ message, code: "request_timeout" }`; a call that gets no response at all for 15 minutes rejects the same way. Neither is retried, since the model may already have run (see [Request timeouts](/rate-limits-and-quotas/#request-timeouts)). Use `try...catch` around the call and loop to handle these failures.

## [](#function-calling) Function Calling

Function calling (also known as tool calling) allows AI models to request data or perform actions by calling functions you define. This enables the AI to access real-time information, interact with external systems, and perform tasks beyond its training data.

1. **Define tools** \- Create function specifications in the `tools` array passed to `puter.ai.chat()`

2. **AI requests a tool call** \- If the AI determines it needs to call a function, it responds with a `tool_calls` array instead of a text message

3. **Execute the function** \- Your code matches the requested function and runs it with the provided arguments

4. **Send the result back** \- Pass the function result back to the AI with `role: "tool"`

5. **AI responds** \- The AI uses the tool result to generate its final response

Tools are defined in the `tools` parameter as an array of function specifications:

- `type` (String) \- Must be `"function"`

- `function.name` (String) \- The function name (e.g., `"get_weather"`)

- `function.description` (String) \- Description of what the function does and when to use it

- `function.parameters` (Object) \- [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) object defining the function's input arguments

- `function.strict` (Boolean) (Optional) \- Whether to enforce strict parameter validation

When the AI wants to call a function, the response includes `message.tool_calls`. Each tool call contains:

- `id` (String) \- Unique identifier for this tool call (used when sending results back)

- `function.name` (String) \- The name of the function to call

- `function.arguments` (String) \- JSON string containing the function arguments

After executing the function, send the result back by including a message with:

- `role` (String) \- Must be `"tool"`

- `tool_call_id` (String) \- The `id` from the tool call

- `content` (String) \- The function result as a string

See also [Gemini models](#gemini-models).

See the [Function Calling example](/playground/ai-function-calling/) for a complete working implementation.

## [](#compaction) Compaction

For long, multi-turn conversations that you keep on the client, enable `compaction` so the model can summarize earlier context before it overflows the context window. When it fires, the model summarizes the older turns into a single **compaction artifact** and answers from that summary instead of the full history — so the request stays small.

You get the artifact back as a `compaction` item (a stream chunk when streaming, or `result.compaction` when not). On the next turn you carry it forward **as the first block of the assistant turn that produced it**, together with that turn's reply text — the artifact stands in for the older turns it summarized, and the recent exchange is preserved. The item shape is the same across providers, so the same code works for OpenAI and Anthropic models.

#### [](#enabling-it) Enabling it

Pass `compaction` in the options object:

- `compaction: true` — enable with provider defaults.

- `compaction: { trigger_tokens: 60000 }` — set the token threshold at which the model compacts.

The artifact is `{ type: 'compaction', id, encrypted_content }`. `encrypted_content` is an opaque payload; treat it as a black box and just carry it forward.

#### [](#streaming) Streaming

```js
const resp = await puter.ai.chat(messages, {
    model: 'gpt-5.5',                       // or 'claude-opus-4-8' — same code
    stream: true,
    compaction: { trigger_tokens: 60000 },
});

let text = '';
let compaction = null;
for await ( const part of resp ) {
    if ( part.type === 'text' )             text += part.text;
    else if ( part.type === 'compaction' )  compaction = part;                 // { type, id, encrypted_content }
    else if ( part.type === 'error' )       console.error('stream error:', part.message);
}

// Next turn: rebuild the assistant turn from the compaction artifact + the reply
// text it came with (artifact first), then add the new user message. The artifact
// replaces the older compacted turns; the recent exchange is kept. Keep
// compaction enabled so it can compact again later.
if ( compaction ) {
    const next = await puter.ai.chat(
        [
            { role: 'system', content: 'You are a helpful assistant.' },
            {
                role: 'assistant',
                content: [ compaction, { type: 'text', text } ],
            },
            { role: 'user', content: 'now compare the two approaches' },
        ],
        { model: 'gpt-5.5', stream: true, compaction: true }
    );
    for await ( const part of next ) {
        if ( part.type === 'text' ) document.write(part.text);
    }
}
```

#### [](#non-streaming) Non-streaming

```js
const result = await puter.ai.chat(messages, {
    model: 'gpt-5.5',
    compaction: { trigger_tokens: 60000 },
});
console.log(result.message.content);

if ( result.compaction ) {
    // result.compaction is { type: 'compaction', id, encrypted_content } — the
    // same item you get from the stream. Rebuild the assistant turn from it plus
    // the reply text (artifact first), then add the new user message:
    const next = await puter.ai.chat(
        [
            { role: 'system', content: 'You are a helpful assistant.' },
            {
                role: 'assistant',
                content: [
                    result.compaction,
                    { type: 'text', text: result.message.content },
                ],
            },
            { role: 'user', content: 'now compare the two approaches' },
        ],
        { model: 'gpt-5.5', compaction: true }
    );
    console.log(next.message.content);
}
```

#### [](#notes) Notes

- **Keep `compaction` enabled on every turn** of the conversation so it can compact again as the conversation keeps growing.

- **Carry the artifact as the first block of its assistant turn**, alongside that turn's reply text, then continue with new turns. The artifact replaces the older compacted turns; don't drop the recent exchange.

- **It only fires once the context is large enough.** Anthropic models require a minimum threshold of **50,000 tokens**, and the conversation must actually exceed your `trigger_tokens`. OpenAI models don't enforce that floor, so they can compact smaller conversations. If nothing compacts, your input was below the threshold.

- **Handle the `error` chunk** when streaming — provider errors (e.g. a `trigger_tokens` below a provider's minimum) arrive as an `error` chunk, not a thrown exception.

## [](#response-normalization) Response Normalization

Most providers respond in the OpenAI chat format, where `message.content` is a string and tool calls appear as `message.tool_calls`. Anthropic models historically respond in Anthropic's native format instead, where `message.content` is an array of content blocks such as `[{ type: "text", text: "..." }]`.

**Going forward, all models released on or after September 1, 2026 return responses in the OpenAI format**, no matter which provider serves them — so the same response-handling code works across every new model. For models released before that date, the `normalize` default does not change: leave the option unset and `message.content` keeps its provider-native shape.

**Reasoning fields on existing models**

Separately from the `normalize` default, four reasoning-related fields were made consistent across providers. These apply to **every** model, including ones released before the cutoff, and are not affected by `normalize`:

| Field | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message.reasoning_content` | Present on providers following the DeepSeek convention (DeepSeek, OpenRouter and others) | **Renamed to `message.reasoning`.** Read `reasoning` instead — `reasoning_content` is no longer present on non-streaming responses. |
| `message.reasoning` on OpenAI Responses models | Always present as `null` | Absent when the model returned no reasoning summary; a string when it did. `if (msg.reasoning)` is unaffected; `'reasoning' in msg` changes. |
| `message.reasoning_details` on OpenAI Responses models | Not present | Present when the model returned reasoning items, carrying their `id` and `encrypted_content` for replay. |
| `finish_reason` on OpenAI Responses models | Always `"stop"` | `"tool_calls"` when the turn ended in tool calls, `"stop"` otherwise. |

If your code reads `message.reasoning_content` on a non-streaming response, that is the one change that removes a field — switch to `message.reasoning`.

You can control this per call with the `normalize` option:

```js
// Force the OpenAI format on any model, old or new:
const response = await puter.ai.chat("Hello", { model: "claude-sonnet-5", normalize: true });
console.log(response.message.content);   // a string, or null on a tool-only turn
console.log(response.finish_reason);     // "stop" | "length" | "tool_calls" | "content_filter" | provider value

// Force the provider-native format, even on a post-cutoff model:
const native = await puter.ai.chat("Hello", { model: "claude-sonnet-5", normalize: false });
```

Or SDK-wide with `puter.ai.normalize`:

```js
// Unset (the default): the release-date rule applies — models released on or
// after September 1, 2026 return the OpenAI format, older models stay native.
puter.ai.normalize = true;      // force normalization: every chat() call
                                // returns the OpenAI format, old or new model
puter.ai.normalize = false;     // disable normalization: every chat() call
                                // returns the provider-native format
puter.ai.normalize = undefined; // back to the release-date rule
```

A `normalize` option on an individual call always overrides `puter.ai.normalize` in either direction. Normalized responses carry `normalized: true`.

On a normalized response, extended-thinking output (from reasoning models that expose it) is joined into `message.reasoning`, and Anthropic stop reasons are mapped to OpenAI values (`end_turn` → `stop`, `max_tokens` → `length`, `tool_use` → `tool_calls`, `refusal` → `content_filter`). A provider stop reason with no OpenAI equivalent — Anthropic's `pause_turn`, for instance — passes through unchanged, so treat `finish_reason` as an open set. See [`finish_reason`](/Objects/chatresponse) for the full mapping.

Normalization does not cost you the ability to continue a reasoning turn. The opaque parts a provider needs back — Anthropic thinking-block signatures, OpenAI reasoning item ids and encrypted content — are preserved verbatim on `message.reasoning_details`. Resend that array as-is alongside the message when you continue an extended-thinking tool-use loop. The artifacts are provider-specific and only meaningful to the model that produced them, so replay them to the same model — don't carry them across providers. Kimi K3.1 Pro reads its `reasoning` string back the same way, so keep `reasoning` on the assistant message when you continue a conversation with it.

One caveat. The release-date rule applies to the model that actually serves the request — if a request is rerouted to a fallback provider, the served model's release date decides.

One thing to know about the release-date rule: a model's release date comes from the catalog of whichever provider serves it, and some providers report it from their own live listing. Models served through OpenRouter carry the date OpenRouter itself assigns, so a model newly listed there on or after September 1, 2026 is normalized by default without Puter shipping any change. Pin `normalize: false` if your code depends on a provider's native shape.

Streaming is unaffected by normalization: streamed [`ChatResponseChunk`](/Objects/chatresponsechunk) objects already share one format across all providers, and the chunk types a model emits do not depend on the `normalize` option. Reasoning models stream their thinking as `reasoning` chunks on every provider, whether or not normalization applies.

## [](#providers) Providers

We use different providers for different models and try to use the best provider available at the time of the request. Providers currently include Alibaba Cloud, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek, Google, Infron, Meta, MiniMax, Mistral, Moonshot AI, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Together AI, xAI, and Z.AI. Call [`puter.ai.listModelProviders()`](/AI/listModelProviders) for the current list, or pass `provider` in the options object to pin a request to one of them.

When the provider serving a request fails, Puter retries the request on the next provider that serves the same model (up to three attempts), and you are billed for the attempt that answers. Pass `fallback: false` to turn this off, so that a failure from the first provider tried is returned to you instead:

```js
// Answered by Anthropic directly, or an error. Never sent to another provider.
const response = await puter.ai.chat('Hello', {
    model: 'claude-sonnet-4-6',
    provider: 'claude',
    fallback: false,
});
```

With `provider` set as well, the request is answered by that provider or fails. If that provider does not serve the model, the request fails with a `400` instead of going to another provider. The error is the same one you would get if every provider had failed, for example `400 upstream_provider_unavailable` or `429 upstream_rate_limited`.

## [](#service-speed) Service speed

The `serviceSpeed` option selects service capacity independently of reasoning effort. If the requested speed is unavailable for the selected model, the request uses the next supported speed in the order `ultrafast`, `fast`, `standard`.

A faster tier that rejects a request because its capacity or access is unavailable can retry at a lower speed on the same provider. The `fallback` option controls retries on other providers separately. Once streaming output starts, a failed stream ends with an error instead of restarting at another speed.

The `usageDetails.serviceSpeed` field reports the served speed. Billing uses the tier or equivalent model that served the request. A provider downgrade is billed at the lower tier's rates. Response normalization follows the same rule as a request without this option, including when a faster equivalent model is selected.

## [](#model-specific-features) Model-specific features

### [](#openai-models) OpenAI models

Passing `service_tier: "priority"` selects fast service, and `service_tier: "ultrafast"` selects ultrafast service. These requests use the same prices and supported-speed selection as `serviceSpeed`. An explicit `serviceSpeed` takes precedence.

Input and reasoning tokens reported by a non-streaming Responses API call are billed even when its output is empty. These charges apply whether the request fails or retries another provider.

Fast service is available on models with a published Fast rate card. Ultrafast is available for GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra. Other models fall back to fast or standard. Cache and long-context rates apply to the served tier.

#### [](#temperature) `temperature`

Some OpenAI reasoning models ignore `temperature` and `top_p`. GPT-5.6, GPT-6 Sol/Luna, and GPT-6.1 Terra accept them only with `reasoning_effort: 'none'`, and GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-5.3 Codex always ignore them.

#### [](#reasoning_effort) `reasoning_effort`

GPT-6.1 Terra accepts `none`, `low`, `medium` (default), `high`, `xhigh`, and `max`.

#### [](#web-search) Web Search

Specific to OpenAI models, you can use the built-in web search tool, allowing the AI to access up-to-date information from the internet.

Pass in the `tools` parameter with the type of `web_search`.

```js
{
  model: 'openai/gpt-6-luna',
  tools: [{type: "web_search"}]
}
```

The code implementation is available in our [web search example](/playground/ai-web-search/).

List of OpenAI models that support the web search can be found in their [API compatibility documentation](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/tools-web-search#api-compatibility).

#### [](#prompt-caching) Prompt Caching

OpenAI models cache prompt prefixes on their own. Requests from the same app and user share one cache by default, and you can pick the cache with `prompt_cache_key`. Their `usage` reports the tokens read from the cache as `cached_tokens`.

GPT-5.6 and later models charge for cache writes and let you choose how long an entry lives. Pass `prompt_cache_options` with a `ttl` of `"30m"` (the default) or `"12h"`. The `usage` reports the tokens written with the 30 minute lifetime as `cache_write_tokens` and the tokens written with the 12 hour lifetime as `cache_write_12h_tokens`. Writing a 30 minute entry costs 1\.25 times the model's input rate, and writing a 12 hour entry costs 2\.5 times the input rate. Reads cost the same for both lifetimes. To mark where a reusable prefix ends, add `prompt_cache_breakpoint: { mode: "explicit" }` to a content part. A breakpoint can carry its own `ttl`, which overrides the request's. OpenAI only takes a 12 hour lifetime, or a lifetime on a breakpoint, through its Responses API, so a request that uses either is sent there.

```js
puter.ai.chat('<your message>', {
    model: 'gpt-6-luna',
    prompt_cache_options: { ttl: '12h' }
});
```

Older OpenAI models charge nothing for cache writes. Pass `prompt_cache_retention` with `"in_memory"` for an entry that lives a few minutes or `"24h"` for one that can live up to a day. The 24 hour option is the default, and GPT-5.5 and later models only support it.

The `usageDetails` object on every result carries the same counts under provider-neutral names, with one field per lifetime, such as `cacheWrite30mTokens` and `cacheWrite12hTokens`. See the [ChatResponse](/Objects/chatresponse/) object for the full list.

### [](#anthropic-models) Anthropic models

Fast service is available on Claude models with a Fast rate card. Ultrafast falls back to fast. When the account has no Fast quota, the request retries at standard speed. The upstream service tier and inference speed are separate fields.

Pass `speed: "fast"` to request Fast mode, or `speed: "standard"` for standard inference. This option applies to Claude models. An explicit `serviceSpeed` takes precedence.

#### [](#prompt-caching-1) Prompt Caching

Specific to Anthropic models, you can use the cache control feature, allowing you to optimize costs for repeated prompts.

Pass in the `cache_control` parameter inside the object in the `messages` array.

```js
[
    {
        role: 'system',
        content: 'a really long system prompt',
        cache_control: { type: "ephemeral" }
    },
    {
        role: 'user',
        content: '<your message>'
    },
]
```

You can find the implementation in our [prompt caching example](/playground/ai-claude-cache-control/). Find more details about cache control in [Anthropic documentation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching).

### [](#gemini-models) Gemini models

Fast service uses Priority inference on supported text and image requests. Other media use standard service to preserve input handling.

#### [](#temperature-1) `temperature`

Gemini 4 Carbon (`gemini-4-carbon`), Gemini 4 Argon (`gemini-4-argon`) and Gemini 4 Hydrogen (`gemini-4-hydrogen`) ignore `temperature`. The `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` and `gemini-3-flash-preview` models use it.

#### [](#reasoning_effort-1) `reasoning_effort`

Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon accept `low`, `medium` and `high`, and use `medium` when you leave it unset. Gemini 4 Hydrogen accepts `low`, `medium`, `high` and `xhigh`, and uses `high` when you leave it unset. The `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` and `gemini-3-flash-preview` models accept `minimal`, `low`, `medium` and `high`, and use Google's default level when you leave it unset. For these five Gemini models, any other value fails with `400 bad_request`, and messages can contain text and images only.

The other Gemini models ignore `reasoning_effort`.

#### [](#function-calling-1) Function calling

Gemini models can attach `extra_content.google.thought_signature` to a tool call. Send the assistant message back with its `tool_calls` unchanged, including `extra_content`, so the model can continue its reasoning. In a stream, the signature arrives on the `tool_use` chunk's `extra_content`.

### [](#gemini-image-models) Gemini image models

Certain Gemini models can generate and edit images as part of a chat conversation. These models accept text and image inputs, and return text and images in the response.

#### [](#supported-models) Supported Models

| Model | Quality Levels |
| --- | --- |
| `gemini-3-pro-image-preview` | `1K`, `2K`, `4K` |
| `gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview` | `512`, `1K`, `2K`, `4K` |

#### [](#options) Options

Pass `image_config` in the options object to control image output:

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `image_config.aspect_ratio` | `String` | Aspect ratio (e.g. `"16:9"`, `"1:1"`, `"9:16"`) |
| `image_config.image_size` | `String` | Output quality/resolution. Must be one of the model's supported quality levels |

For available aspect ratios and image sizes per model, see the [Gemini Image Generation documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/image-generation#aspect_ratios_and_image_size).

#### [](#response-format) Response Format

The response includes an `images` array on the message when the model generates images:

```js
{
    message: {
        role: "assistant",
        content: "Here is your image.",
        images: [
            {
                type: "image_url",
                image_url: { url: "data:image/png;base64,..." }
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

#### [](#multi-turn-image-editing) Multi-Turn Image Editing

You can send generated images back in the conversation to iteratively edit them. Include the image in an `assistant` message using the `image_url` content type, and pass the `thoughtSignature` from the previous response to maintain editing context:

```js
const previousImage = result.message.images[0].image_url.url;
const thoughtSignature = result.message.images[0].thoughtSignature;

const result2 = await puter.ai.chat([
    { role: "user", content: "Create an infographic about photosynthesis" },
    { role: "assistant", content: [
        { type: "text", text: "Here is the infographic." },
        { type: "image_url", image_url: { url: previousImage }, thoughtSignature },
    ]},
    { role: "user", content: "Translate all text to Spanish" },
], {
    model: "gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview",
    image_config: { aspect_ratio: "16:9", image_size: "2K" },
});

const editedImage = result2.message.images[0].image_url.url;
```

The code implementation is available in our [image generation example](/playground/ai-image-chat/) and [multi-turn image editing example](/playground/ai-image-edit/).

#### [](#streaming-1) Streaming

Image generation works with `stream: true`. Image chunks arrive as `image` events:

```js
const resp = await puter.ai.chat("Draw a cat", {
    model: "gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview",
    stream: true,
});

for await (const part of resp) {
    if (part.text) console.log(part.text);
    if (part.image) {
        // part.image is { type: "image_url", image_url: { url: "data:..." } }
        const img = document.createElement("img");
        img.src = part.image.image_url.url;
        document.body.appendChild(img);
    }
}
```

### [](#moonshot-kimi-models) Moonshot Kimi models

Models with an equivalent Highspeed variant select that variant for fast service. Other models use standard service.

#### [](#reasoning_effort-2) `reasoning_effort`

Kimi K3.1 Pro accepts `low`, `high` and `max`, uses `max` when you leave it unset, and fails with `400 bad_request` on any other value. The other Kimi models ignore `reasoning_effort`.

#### [](#prompt-caching-2) Prompt Caching

Moonshot's Kimi K3 and Kimi K3.1 Pro models cache prompt prefixes on their own and take no `cache_control`. Their `usage` reports the tokens read from the cache as `cached_tokens` and the tokens written to it as `cache_write_tokens`. Each is billed at the model's own rate from the [AI models list](https://developer.puter.com/ai/models/).

### [](#meta-muse-spark-models) Meta Muse Spark models

#### [](#reasoning_effort-3) `reasoning_effort`

Muse Spark always reasons, so `none` is ignored for it.

### [](#xai-models) xAI models

Fast service requests Priority processing. Token charges, including cached input and reasoning, follow the served tier.

### [](#minimax-models) MiniMax models

MiniMax M3 uses Priority admission for fast service. Earlier models with an equivalent Highspeed variant use that variant. Other models use standard service.

### [](#mistral-models) Mistral models

Fast service requests Priority when the account and model are eligible. The provider can serve the request at standard speed.

Passing `service_tier: "auto"` selects fast service, with the same prices as `serviceSpeed: "fast"`. An explicit `serviceSpeed` takes precedence.

### [](#alibaba-cloud-models) Alibaba Cloud models

Models with an equivalent Prime or Fast variant select that variant for fast service. Other models use standard service.

### [](#openrouter-models) OpenRouter models

Faster tiers come from the selected model's endpoint catalog. A tier can fall back upstream. Billing uses the endpoint that serves the request.

### [](#infron-models) Infron models

Models with a Priority offering select that offering for fast service. Other models use standard service.

## Objective
- Build a Python FastAPI backend + lightweight web UI for an AI-powered agricultural decision-support app that recommends crops to farmers worldwide using NASA POWER data.
- Latest focus: farmer-friendly Streamlit UI (map parcel pick, browser geolocation, free-text "ne ekeyim?", optional detail checkbox) plus evaluating Puter.js as an alternative Gemini access path.

## Requirements
- Everything lives in `C:\Users\moyil\Desktop\Project Alphecca`.
- Python-based; user dislikes raw HTML/CSS (accepts minimal HTML where unavoidable, e.g. geolocation page).
- Backend must be testable, runnable, documented (`README.md`, `RAPOR.md`).
- Use NASA APIs for climate/soil/weather; AI evaluates farmer input and recommends crops.
- Rules must be strict so AI cannot make dangerous agronomic mistakes.
- Conceptual answers must be verbal (sözel), not only files.
- UI must suit low-education farmers: very simple, short sentences, big flow.
- Detail (climate/soil/score) hidden behind a checkbox, off by default.
- Map API for parcel selection; if not possible, browser geolocation permission.
- User asked to find the Gemini API online and add it to the code for testing.

## Decisions
- FastAPI + Pydantic v2 + httpx backend; Streamlit UI layered on top (UI only calls HTTP API, no business logic).
- Deterministic 16-crop rule engine is the ranking authority; AI only explains/annotates. `/analyze` uses 65/35 blend; `/advice` has zero AI ranking power (`final_score == rule_score`, `ai_score = None`).
- Advice flow: free text + simple inputs → NASA data → rule ranking → AI plain-language plan → heuristic fallback if no key/error.
- Gemini: `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, `x-goog-api-key` header, `temperature` only for `gemini-2*`.
- Map = `streamlit-folium` + `folium` + OpenStreetMap (no key); reverse geocoding = Nominatim (TTL cache, required User-Agent).
- Browser geolocation via FastAPI-served `/geo` page redirecting with `?lat=..&lon=..` (iframes cannot request geolocation).
- Map center/zoom pinned explicitly in `st_folium` to stop the map jumping to world view on rerun.
- Buttons that mutate widget state use `on_click` callbacks (`_fill_example_text`, `_reset_coordinates`, `_use_preset`).
- Expert/test tabs preserved inside an "Uzman / test modu" expander.

Alternatif: Arpa.", detail checkbox opens climate/soil/monthly table/score table, `?lat=&lon=` geolocation return updates to Tekirdağ.

## [Rate limits  |  Gemini API  |  Google AI for Developers](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits?authuser=0)

## How rate limits work Copy link to this section: How rate limits work

Rate limits are usually measured across three dimensions:

- Requests per minute (RPM)
- Tokens per minute (input) (TPM)
- Requests per day (RPD)

Your usage is evaluated against each limit, and exceeding any of them will trigger a rate limit error. For example, if your RPM limit is 20, making 21 requests within a minute will result in an error, even if you haven't exceeded your TPM or other limits.

Rate limits are applied per project, not per API key. Requests per day (RPD) quotas reset at midnight Pacific time.

Limits vary depending on the specific model being used, and some limits only apply to specific models. For example, Images per minute, or IPM, is only calculated for models capable of generating images (Nano Banana), but is conceptually similar to TPM. Other models might have a token per day limit (TPD). Built-in tools also have specific rate limits. For example, Grounding with Google Search on Gemini 3 and newer models is subject to a default limit of 1,500 requests per day (RPD) per project on the Gemini Developer API (see Grounding with Google Search).

Rate limits are more restricted for experimental and preview models.

...

In addition to requests per minute (RPM) and tokens per minute (TPM) limits, the Gemini API enforces spend-based rate limits to protect against unexpected charges. Whether these limits apply to your account depends on your billing history and usage tier.

## [Gemini's free tier, measured: 20 requests a day, and Google no longer publishes the number](https://aiplug.work/en/blog/gemini-free-tier-limits)
Published: 2026-09-02T07:30:28.000Z

## The numbers

Measured 2026-09-02, on a Google account, project and API key all created that day, with no billing attached:

| Model | RPM | RPD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gemini-3.7-flash` | 5 | 20 |
| `gemini-3.6-flash` | 5 | 20 |
| `gemini-3.5-flash` | 5 | 20 |
| `gemini-3-flash-preview` | 5 | 20 |
| `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | 15 | 500 |
| `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` | 15 | 500 |
| `gemini-embedding-2` | 100 | 1000 |

Two caveats belong with those figures. Quota is counted per project, not per key — minting extra keys in the same project buys you nothing. And RPD resets at midnight Pacific, not at your local midnight.

## Google stopped publishing them

This is not a case of the table being hard to find. The Gemini rate-limits page now contains zero occurrences of the phrase "free tier". Its only tables are spend-based rate limits, the qualification thresholds for each paid tier, and batch quotas for Tiers 1 through 3. There is no free-tier table at all. The prose says limits "can be viewed in Google AI Studio" and that "specified rate limits are not guaranteed". The individual model pages carry no RPM or RPD either.

...

The obvious way to measure a rate limit is to hammer the endpoint until it fails and count what got through. That only ever gives you a lower bound: concurrency, retries and window boundaries all cost you a few requests, and you never learn how many.

You don't need to. When Gemini rejects you, the 429 body contains the limit itself. The error's `details` array carries a `google.rpc.QuotaFailure`, and each violation names the quota and its value:

```
{"quotaMetric": "generativelanguage.googleapis.com/generate_content_free_tier_requests",
 "quotaId": "GenerateRequestsPerDayPerProjectPerModel-FreeTier",
 "quotaDimensions": {"model": "gemini-3.5-flash", "location": "global"},
 "quotaValue": "20"}
```

Trip the limit once and Google hands you the answer. Every figure in the table above was read out this way rather than counted, which makes each one the limit rather than an observed floor — a distinction worth caring about if you plan to design around the number.

Three quota ids are worth knowing: `GenerateRequestsPerMinutePerProjectPerModel-FreeTier` for RPM, `GenerateRequestsPerDayPerProjectPerModel-FreeTier` for RPD, and, for embeddings, `EmbedContentRequestsPerDayPerUserPerProjectPerModel-FreeTier`. Note the extra `PerUser` in the last one — embeddings are metered on a different basis from text generation.

## The real change is where the limit lives

Older Gemini free-tier posts, videos and examples often show a static RPM/RPD table. Google's current rate-limits documentation directs developers to AI Studio for active per-model limits. A published figure from an earlier date is not a promise about your project today.

The mechanics still matter. Limits are usually measured across requests per minute (RPM), input tokens per minute (TPM), and requests per day (RPD). Exceeding any one can trigger an error while the others still have room. Limits apply per project, not per API key, and RPD resets at midnight Pacific time. Some models have additional dimensions, such as images per minute or tokens per day.

There are three separate checks:

1. Model and feature: the pricing page says whether the exact model, mode and tool have free pricing.
2. Project access: project status and eligibility guidance explain whether your account/project can use that free route.
3. Capacity: AI Studio's rate-limit view shows the selected project's active limits.

For example, a free input/output row cannot override a project's “Free tier unavailable” status. A project that is eligible can still exhaust its daily quota. The first needs an access decision; the second needs a quota or traffic decision.

## Is a free Gemini API key unlimited? Auth keys and project limits

The key is free, but it is not unlimited. Google's API key documentation says every key belongs to a Google Cloud project. New AI Studio users get a default project and key after accepting the terms; existing Cloud users can import their projects. Neither flow guarantees that the project qualifies for free inference.

Since May 28, 2026, new keys created in AI Studio are authorization (auth) keys, bound to a service account and restricted to the Gemini API by default. Unrestricted standard keys are rejected; standard keys with appropriate explicit restrictions can still work. Keep credentials on the server and follow Google's key creation and security instructions when importing or replacing a key.

import asyncio
import os
import time

import httpx

KEY = os.environ["PROBE_KEY"]
BASE = "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta"
MODELS = os.environ.get("PROBE_MODELS", "gemini-3.5-flash-lite,gemini-flash-latest").split(",")


async def one(client: httpx.AsyncClient, model: str) -> None:
    payload = {
        "contents": [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": "Reply with the single word: OK"}]}],
        "generationConfig": {"maxOutputTokens": 128},
    }
    started = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        resp = await client.post(
            f"{BASE}/models/{model}:generateContent",
            headers={"x-goog-api-key": KEY, "Content-Type": "application/json"},
            json=payload,
        )
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"{model}: EXC {type(exc).__name__} after {time.perf_counter() - started:.1f}s")
        return
    dt = time.perf_counter() - started
    print(f"{model}: HTTP {resp.status_code} in {dt:.1f}s")
    if resp.status_code == 200:
        data = resp.json()
        try:
            text = "".join(p.get("text", "") for p in data["candidates"][0]["content"]["parts"])
            print("   text:", repr(text[:100]))
        except Exception:
            print("   shape:", str(data)[:200])
    else:
        print("   ", resp.text[:400])


async def main() -> None:
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=90) as client:
        for model in MODELS:
            await one(client, model)


asyncio.run(main())

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import sys
import time

from app.ai.base import AdviceContext
from app.ai.factory import build_ai_provider
from app.ai.heuristic import HeuristicProvider
from app.config import Settings, get_settings

SAMPLE_FREE_TEXT = (
    "Edirne'de 20 dönüm tarlam var, 2 dönümü sulanabiliyor. Ne ekeceğimi bilmiyorum. "
    "Bitkiyi nasıl büyüteceğimi, nasıl besleyeceğimi ve nasıl bakacağımı da bilmiyorum."
)


def build_context(language: str = "tr") -> AdviceContext:
    """Kural motorunun gerçek çıktısına benzeyen küçük, sabit bir bağlam."""

    return AdviceContext(
        language=language,
        location={
            "latitude": 41.6771,
            "longitude": 26.5557,
            "region_name": "Edirne",
        },
        farmer={
            "field": {

                "soil_texture": "clay_loam",
                "soil_ph": 6.8,
                "organic_matter_pct": 1.6,
            },
            "resources": {"irrigation": "limited", "water_availability": "medium"},
            "preferences": {"goal": "max_profit", "planting_month": 10},
        },

                "annual_mean_temp_c": 13.65,
                "annual_precip_mm": 613.0,
                "climate_class": "semi_arid",

            },

        },

                "rule_score": 92.0,
                "why": "Kışı soğuk geçen, 600 mm civarı yağış alan tarlaya uyar.",
                "limiting_factors": ["Kurak ilkbaharda sulama gerekebilir."],
            },
            {
                "crop_key": "barley",
                "local_name": "Arpa",
                "rule_score": 91.2,
                "why": "Buğdaya göre kuraklığa daha dayanıklı.",

            },

                "limiting_factors": ["Çiçeklenmede su stresi verimi düşürür."],
            },
        ],
        free_text=SAMPLE_FREE_TEXT,
        data_quality=[
            "NASA POWER verisi 0.5-1 derece ızgaradır; tarla ölçeğinde değildir.",
            "Toprak pH ve organik madde çiftçi beyanıdır, ölçülmemiştir.",
        ],
    )


def _print_plan(plan) -> None:
    print(f"\nBaşlık: {plan.headline}")
    print(f"Gerekçe: {plan.why}")
    for title, items in (
        ("İlk adımlar", plan.steps),
        ("Nasıl büyütülür", plan.grow),
        ("Nasıl beslenir", plan.feed),
        ("Nasıl bakılır", plan.care),
        ("Riskler", plan.risks),
        ("Çiftçiye sorulacaklar", plan.ask_farmer),
    ):
        if not items:
            continue
        print(f"\n{title}:")
        for item in items:
            print(f"  - {item}")
    print(f"\nGüven: {plan.confidence}")


async def _run(settings: Settings, language: str) -> int:
    provider = build_ai_provider(settings)
    name = getattr(provider, "name", "unknown")
    model = getattr(provider, "model", None)
    print(f"Sağlayıcı : {name}")
    print(f"Model     : {model or '-'}")
    print(f"Anahtar   : {'tanımlı' if settings.ai_api_key else 'YOK'}")

    if isinstance(provider, HeuristicProvider):
        print("\nAI devrede değil; deterministik motor kullanılıyor.")
        if provider.reason:
            print(f"Sebep: {provider.reason}")
        print("İpucu: .env içinde AI_PROVIDER=gemini ve AI_API_KEY=... olmalı.")
        return 1

    context = build_context(language)
    started = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        plan = await provider.advise(context)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - CLI diagnostics
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
        print(f"\nHATA ({elapsed:.1f} sn): {exc}")
        return 1
    finally:
        close = getattr(provider, "aclose", None)
        if callable(close):
            await close()

    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
    print(f"Gecikme   : {elapsed:.2f} sn")
    _print_plan(plan)

    if not plan.headline:
        print("\nUYARI: başlık boş döndü; model JSON şemasına tam uymamış olabilir.")
        return 1
    print("\nOK: gerçek AI cevabı alındı ve doğrulamadan geçti.")
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Project Alphecca canlı AI kontrolü")
    parser.add_argument("--provider", help="AI_PROVIDER değerini geçici olarak değiştir")
    parser.add_argument("--model", help="AI_MODEL değerini geçici olarak değiştir")
    parser.add_argument("--language", default="tr", choices=["tr", "en"])
    args = parser.parse_args()

    settings = get_settings()
    if args.provider:
        settings.ai_provider = args.provider
    if args.model:
        settings.ai_model = args.model

    return asyncio.run(_run(settings, args.language))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
